::: {#def-marginal-likelihood}
#### Marginal likelihood (evidence)

Given a prior $\p(\param)$
and a model $\p(\vy \mid \param)$ for the data given $\param$,
the **marginal likelihood**
[@wikipedia_marginal_likelihood] (also called the **evidence**)
of observed data $\vy$ is

$$
\p(\vy) \eqdef \int \p(\vy \mid \param)\, \p(\param)\, d\param,
$$

with the integral replaced by a sum over the possible values of $\param$
when $\param$ is discrete.
:::
